findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker was reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This looks like a leftover debugging change unrelated to the deadlock fix. All cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, annotations, query history and others) will run 10x more often. Each run can last up to the 9 minute timeout, so runs may nearly back to back and add DB load. Revert it to 10 minutes.

findings.title: Debug logging at Error level that dumps all IDs on every batch
findings.body: Each batch logs at Error level, including the full `ids` slice (up to the batch size, which may be tens of thousands of IDs) and the condition. This also happens when nothing was found. The same pattern appears at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579. It floods error logs and triggers alerting on error logs during normal operation. Use Debug level and drop the ID list. Also, the 'err' value logged is always nil at that point.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit check uses configured batch size and misses the placeholder cap
findings.body: The inline-ID branch triggers only when the configured batch size is above 999. The decision should be based on len(ids). With a small configured value the placeholders path is fine, but the check depends on config rather than on the actual number of parameters. Also, for MaxCount cleanup, LimitOffset may return up to the batch size, so the logic is consistent only by coincidence. Prefer checking len(ids).

findings.title: Orphan tag cleanup condition is ambiguous inside fetchIDs
findings.body: The condition `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM annotation a WHERE annotation_id = a.id)` is now used in `SELECT id FROM annotation_tag WHERE ...`. The unqualified `annotation_id` resolves to annotation_tag only because annotation has no such column, which is fragile. More importantly, the `id` column of annotation_tag is used for the delete. That is correct only if the table has an id column, so verify that it does.
